text:
Ravi Patel: Heads-up: hitting RuntimeError: Event loop is closed when running our async SDK in notebook + pytest. Stack shows atexit handler calling run_until_complete during shutdown.

Leah M.: can you share a tiny repro? Is the client created at import/top-level?

Ravi Patel: yep, top-level in a notebook. Minimal: create AsyncClient(), await client.embed(...), then restart kernel -> traceback on exit.

Tom H.: this is the old auto-close via atexit. We should not call loop.run_until_complete at interpreter shutdown. That breaks when pytest-asyncio or jupyter owns the loop.

Leah M.: suggested fix: remove atexit blocking close; use weakref.finalize to log a warning and in __del__ try to schedule aclose with get_running_loop + create_task, otherwise log. Make client.aclose idempotent.

Ravi Patel: also add docs: patterns for notebooks, pytest, and FastAPI lifespan. Add typing stub so `async with AsyncClient()` doesn't trigger mypy/flake errors.

Tom H.: will open PR + small CI test that simulates pytest teardown to prevent regression. Deploy Bot: Issue #2410 created (labels: sdk, async, bug).

Leah M.: nice, thanks. Migration note: if you relied on implicit process-exit close, switch to explicit await client.aclose() or async with. :thumbsup:
